label: <DEL> step of long sequences whose first token is d/i/a/s/v/u/b/y
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step (97% of activation mass; 16% of <DEL> steps are active); it never fires during the copy phase. Two things set magnitude. (1) Sequence length: the rate at <DEL> rises steeply with L (about 0 for L<=4, 7.5% of all steps at t=8-9 for L=8-9). (2) The first original token (the token about to be output): d is strongest (lift 8x, 25% of mass), then i, a, s, v, u, b, y, and p/0/c are weak. All top activations are length-8/9 sequences that start with d. Weak precursor activations (about 3% of mass) also appear on the last 1-2 original tokens just before <DEL> in long sequences. Neither the identity of the other tokens nor the digit count matters much. The predicate (delimiter, L>=7, first token in that set) has dev precision 0.83, recall 0.63, mass recall 0.84. It misses weak firings on other first tokens and shorter sequences, so the dependence is graded rather than a clean boolean.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: d, i, a, s, v, u; least: x, z, e, o) and the third original token (most: z, n, x, 1, e, 2; least: b, p, a, d); timing cues that raise it most: t=8, t=7, L=9 & t=8.
